name: Hungary
period: Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04
scope: Hungary national institutions and implemented policy through2026-10-04, including local/nationality variation; not citizens’ attitudes. Announced reforms distinguished from enactment and delivered outcomes.
brief: April2026 competitive election produced a May9 change of prime minister; emergency decree rule ended and July constitutional changes altered judicial and office rules.
counterEvidence: Earlier uneven campaigning and captured institutions are relevant inherited constraints, not evidence Orbán remains prime minister. Supermajority reform and stated independence do not prove every court now practically independent.

answers.rationale: April12 competitive election replaced the governing majority and May9 parliamentary election installed a new prime minister; national elections recur constitutionally.
Electoral and parliamentary selection, not an expert panel, determines national government.
Adult suffrage is not education/intelligence-qualified; judicial disqualification and capacity exceptions qualify universality.
Ordinary legislation requires parliament, and emergency decree governance ended in May. A parliamentary rejection cannot simply be overridden by the prime minister.

Educated assumption: Opposition parties can contest and the2026 transfer demonstrates real competition, but inherited media/resource inequalities qualify equal conditions. Post-transition equality across all campaign resources has not been fully measured.

Educated assumption: Parliamentary oversight, constitutional public-finance disclosure and current investigations support opposition scrutiny. Actual completeness of opposition access after May remains unmeasured, so agreement is moderate.

Educated assumption: Constitutional review can invalidate unlawful governmental action and July reforms change appointments/terms. Earlier political dependence prevents assuming fully independent implementation immediately; moderate agreement weighs enforceable machinery and inherited constraints.
Trade unions do not replace citizens and parliamentary elections in selecting national government.

Educated assumption: Party competition and lawful electoral framework make discretionary ideological exclusion by governing leadership unlikely. Exact current party-dissolution safeguards were not exhaustively traced; unlawful parties are not unrestricted political-position bans.

Article8 permits binding national referendums initiated by200000 voters on parliamentary matters, with turnout and constitutional/budget/treaty exclusions. Repeal can be sought within this qualified scope.
National legislation, budget and constitutional review involve parliament and courts, rather than sole prime-minister authority.
Article21 provides constructive no-confidence initiated by one-fifth of representatives and adopted by an absolute majority electing a replacement prime minister.
Scheduled elections have constitutional procedures; a leader’s personal continuity preference supplies no unilateral postponement authority.

Educated assumption: Representative fixed terms and constitutional local dissolution mechanisms do not establish a voter-initiated individual recall. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; every separate current recall statute was not exhaustively searched.
Electoral replacement and parliamentary confidence demonstrate accountability to elected representatives and voters.
Civilian constitutional command does not authorize military replacement of government on the forces’ own judgment.

name: Indonesia
period: Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04
scope: National institutions and implemented policy through 2026-10-04, with Aceh, customary and regional variation qualified; not citizens’ attitudes. Proposals, signature, registration and construction starts are distinguished from enacted or delivered outcomes.
brief: Competitive direct elections and defined impeachment coexist with elite coalitions, unequal political resources and military administrative influence.
counterEvidence: Actual August2026 constitutional review invalidated government-insult provisions; neither broad coalitions nor military influence establish lawful unilateral executive or military replacement.

answers.rationale: The Constitution provides direct competitive presidential elections and a five-year term renewable once;2024 election selected the current president.
Direct electorate and elected institutions select government, not an expert panel.

Educated assumption: Adult voting is not qualified by education or intelligence. Registration and implementation obstacles qualify universality; every current disenfranchisement exception was not retrieved.

Article20 requires DPR agreement for laws; Article22 emergency regulations require subsequent DPR approval and revocation on rejection. Neither permits an ordinary presidential override of a parliamentary rejection.

Educated assumption: Opposition parties contest elections, but broad incumbent coalitions and resource/media inequalities weaken equal conditions. Moderate agreement best fits competition with unequal practical access; current equality is not comprehensively measured.

Educated assumption: DPR oversight and budget powers support investigation by elected opposition representatives, qualified by coalition dominance and patronage. Exact access to all investigatory records remains unverified.
The Constitutional Court actually voided government-insult Articles240/241 in August2026; constitutional judicial review exists despite documented appointment and independence concerns.
Trade-union leaders do not replace citizens in national government selection.

Educated assumption: Legal restrictions on communist organizations and party registration coexist with constitutional competition and review. These are not general discretionary presidential power to exclude any political position; complete current dissolution procedure remains qualified.

Educated assumption: National lawmaking and constitutional amendment use representative institutions rather than a general voter repeal referendum. No current binding popular-repeal mechanism was located; special regional arrangements do not prove national repeal.
Legislation, budgets and impeachment involve DPR, MPR and courts, rather than sole national-leader authority.
Articles7A/7B allow defined DPR-initiated, Constitutional-Court-tested MPR removal for serious misconduct; this is presidential impeachment, not ordinary parliamentary no-confidence.
The five-year elected term and constitutional election framework do not authorize personal continuity-based unilateral postponement.

Educated assumption: Party replacement and representative removal are not voter-initiated individual recall. Moderate disagreement is likeliest because no general national recall vote was found; complete subnational exceptions remain unverified.
Direct elections, legislative scrutiny and defined impeachment provide constitutional accountability, although implementation weaknesses remain.
Civilian constitutional institutions authorize government; military influence or expanded administrative postings do not grant the armed forces an independent right to replace it.

name: Iran
period: Contemporary institutions and implemented policy; intended cut-off 2026-10-04
scope: National institutions and implemented policy through2026-10-04, not citizens’ attitudes. Supreme leadership distinguished from the elected presidency, actual current war controls from historical laws, and announced measures from completed delivery.
brief: Vetted elections and an elected presidency coexist with supreme clerical authority and constrained opposition. Focused review prioritises implemented competitive renewal and effective oversight; formal powers in controlled institutions are not automatically democratic accountability.
counterEvidence: The March2026 succession used the Assembly of Experts; the president, supreme leader and armed forces have different constitutional powers, so restrictions are not assigned from a generic autocracy label. The bank also credits rejection of specific unelected alternatives (experts, unions, military) and narrower formal rights. These literal answers are retained where supported; the resulting percentage is not a probability or validated democracy index. Restrictions on women inform political participation where relevant, without automatically transferring Authority vs Liberty scores.

answers.rationale: Educated assumption: Regular vetted presidential elections cannot renew or remove the supreme authority through genuinely competitive elections. Supreme leadership, not merely the subordinate presidency, is relevant to national leaders. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.

An elected clerical Assembly of Experts selects ultimate leadership, while the electorate selects a heavily vetted president. Expert-mediated selection and direct election coexist, not one universal government-selection method.

Educated assumption: Ordinary adult suffrage is not education/intelligence-qualified, though candidate eligibility is restrictive. Exact current voter disqualification exceptions were not exhaustively retrieved; candidate vetting is not itself a voter test.

Presidential legislation requires parliament and Guardian Council scrutiny. Supreme-leader/exigency exceptional powers qualify disagreement, but the president is not constitutionally free to enact ordinary laws after parliamentary rejection.
Guardian Council ideological/religious vetting and exclusion of system opponents prevent equal opposition conditions; competition between accepted candidates is narrower.

Educated assumption: Article 76 parliamentary investigation does not give independent opposition access to the protected supreme-leader institutions and state-linked foundations. Exclusion of genuine opposition and immunity from scrutiny outweigh the formal investigative provision. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.

Educated assumption: Constitutional review exists, but the supreme leader appoints the judicial head and controls Guardian Council selection. These dependent institutions do not supply the independent constitutional check required by the statement. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.
Trade-union leaders do not select national government; elected presidency and clerical leadership mechanisms are separate.
Guardian Council qualification screening excludes candidates based on loyalty/religious-political criteria within the governing leadership structure.

Educated assumption: Articles 59 and 110 make referendums dependent on parliamentary supermajority and leadership decree. This is not an implemented voter-controlled power to repeal a law; disagreement is qualified by the existence of binding institution-initiated referendums. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.

Educated assumption: Article 110 places general policy and decisive appointments under supreme leadership. Subordinate executive and parliamentary work does not establish an independent veto over that paramount policy authority. The plural national leadership is assessed, without claiming the president alone decides everything. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.
Articles89/110 provide parliamentary no-confidence findings and supreme-leader implementation of presidential removal; elected representatives have a defined role, not unilateral removal power.
Article68 war postponement requires presidential proposal, three-fourths parliamentary approval and Guardian endorsement. Personal political continuity is not unilateral postponement authority.
Educated assumption: Representative terms and political removal do not establish an individual voter recall vote. Moderate disagreement is likeliest; every council-level exception was not retrieved.

Educated assumption: Supreme authority is insulated from effective voter sanction; vetted representatives and the formal Experts removal provision do not establish independent accountability in practice. Internal clerical selection and removal are not equivalent to accountable popular representation. This interprets implemented institutions, not an official questionnaire response; the exact normative preference is inferred.
Constitutional supreme leadership commands the forces; IRGC influence does not authorize a unilateral military replacement on its own fitness judgment.
